findings.reason: a worker implementing the once-per-pass shape the count sentence permits meets a red assertion on its own deliverable and must choose between two clauses of one section, where deleting the stale half of the count sentence (the write paths already confine the fix to the ledger) makes the gate single-valued.
findings.text: the done-when names two mutually exclusive acceptable shapes for one measure: "a fix serving `run_ids` from a stat-validated cache counts zero and a fix reading once per pass counts one" sits under a bar of "at most once per project", so a once-per-pass fix reads as satisfying the count, while the clause added beside it ("After the pass, a direct `ledger.run_ids(project)` call opens no aggregate read, so the cache serves every caller, not only the tick") fails exactly that shape, because a once-per-pass memo is cold for the direct call and opens one aggregate read
